rationale: Depreciation-to-price is a genuinely less-explored capital-intensity value proxy and the gate (oibdp − dp = post-depreciation operating income) is internally coherent with the stated hypothesis, though the signal remains structurally close to the archive's asset-cheapness × profitability family and risks loading mostly on capital intensity rather than mispricing.

Dividend yield × profitability is essentially the well-documented "dividend safety / high-yield quality" screen, and mechanically dvc is zero or missing for most firms, so the rank product collapses to a large tied mass and the signal is effectively profitability among payers only.

This reuses the archive's Net-Cash Profitable Value first term verbatim and merely swaps the profitability level for its second difference (a construction already probed via TREND in Reactivating Asset Value), making it a cosmetic variant that also replaces the archive's only positive-alpha component with a noisier estimator.

SG&A-to-price as an organizational-capital value proxy conditioned on rising gross profit per unit of SG&A is a substantively distinct construction from the archive's revenue- and asset-based value gates, and the expression matches the hypothesis with a coherent positive sign, with the main caveat that xsga/price will be materially correlated with sales-to-price.

Asset-to-market × high, stable gross margin is close to the canonical value-plus-gross-profitability combination and recombines two already-tested archive components (Reactivating Asset Value's at/mve gate and Durable Cash-Flow Value's level-plus-stability SUMRANK), while a 3-period VOL of annual margins is too short to measure stability reliably.

This is the short-side mirror of the standard value-meets-quality trade ("expensive junk underperforms") and a near-duplicate of the archive's Glamour Profit Fade with the profitability delta swapped for level-plus-volatility, so it adds little beyond an already-tested and statistically weak construction.
